summary: Stepwise revert and traffic-fallback for correctness and latency regressions after enabling adaptive-batching + INT8 profile
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPost Health enabled an adaptive-batching profile alongside an INT8 quantization profile last night for a high-throughput route. Since then they report intermittent correctness drops (short hallucinations in structured outputs) and elevated p95/p99 latency spikes. No full 5xx outage, but a measurable degradation in tail latency and output accuracy for production traffic.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for the affected API route show schema mismatches or truncated fields compared to baseline tests.
- p95 increased from 120ms to 520ms; p99 spiked to ~1.4s intermittently.
- Customer is on Dedicated with reserved GPU pool; business impact: downstream clinical alerts delayed.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity; prod | us-east region
- Route: /v1/generate/structured-alert
- Model pinned at redwood-open-7b-int8 (variant enabled via quant profile); fallback variant redwood-open-7b-ptq available
- Recent changes: adaptive-batching policy (aggressive max-batch-size + dynamic-queueing) + INT8 quant profile staged at 03:00 UTC 2026-03-13

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send 10k representative production requests to /v1/generate/structured-alert over 30 minutes.
2) Compare structured output schema pass rate vs snapshot from 2026-03-12.
3) Observe p95 and p99 latency deltas and intermittent truncated fields in JSON output.

Logs & Telemetry attached by customer:
- Sample request/response pairs included below in comments.
- Trace IDs: trace-20260313-07a9ef, trace-20260313-0b4d12

Requested outcome:
- A safe, stepwise rollback plan the customer can follow that minimizes live-request loss and provides a traffic-split fallback while engineering confirms root cause.
- If feasible, an automated toggle command or console steps the customer can use to ramp back to baseline without purging KV caches unnecessarily.
comments: 2026-03-13 08:12 - Samantha Liu (Support): Logged initial report from customer; collected traces and example payloads. Escalated to SRE for telemetry review. Assigned to Leo Martinez for triage.

2026-03-13 08:35 - Leo Martinez (SRE): Confirmed p95/p99 jumps in tenant-specific latency dashboards coincident with optimizer toggle timestamp. No GPU OOMs. Noted increase in kernel-related retries on the INT8 path. Adding optimizer and scheduler teams to thread.

2026-03-13 09:05 - Customer (BrightPost): Provided two failing responses; one shows truncated JSON field 'clinical_note' and one with schema mismatch. Customer requests a non-disruptive fallback to previous quant profile while retaining batching settings if possible.

2026-03-13 11:20 - Priya Raman (Optimizer Eng): Hypothesis: mixed-lane scheduling combined with INT8 kernel path causes increased decode stalls under certain prompt distributions; will try a canary demote of quant profile on 1 instance group and validate.
2026-03-13 14:45 - Leo Martinez (SRE): Ran preflight checklist and prepared stepwise traffic-split plan. Posting recommended steps below.
investigation_notes:
Telemetry: correlated latency spikes with times when batches exceeded 48 tokens and when adaptive-batcher coalesced heterogeneous requests (short + long sequences) into single batches. Kernel logs show a higher rate of fallback executions on the INT8 execution path (approx 0.8% -> 3.7% fallback invocations). Accuracy: post-quantization token probabilities shifted in specific tokens that generate structured delimiters, leading to truncation of trailing fields. No evidence of disk or network issues.
Repro: Small-scale replay of problematic trace (n=500) reproduced p95 increase when quant profile was active; disabling quant profile on the same host removed truncation behavior and reduced p95 by ~260ms.
Hypotheses: 1) INT8 kernels interacting with batching ordering produce occasional decode stalls/truncation. 2) Aggressive adaptive-batching increases effective sequence packing leading to edge-case tokenization timing that stresses the INT8 path.
Next steps: recommend stepwise rollback prioritizing correctness: demote quant profile per-host, then reduce adaptive-batcher max-batch-size, with traffic-split to fallback PTQ variant while telemetry is observed.
resolution:
Planned mitigation steps provided to customer and ops: 1) Create a 90/10 traffic-split pushing 90% to fallback model redwood-open-7b-ptq and 10% to current INT8 path for 20 minutes. 2) On tenant's dedicated pool, demote INT8 quant profile to 'staged' on one instance group using optimizer-toggle --tenant brightpost --group ig-1 --quant-profile staged (ops-only). 3) Monitor p95/p99 and schema-pass rate for 15 minutes; if stable, progressively increase traffic migration in 10% increments every 10 minutes until 100% on PTQ. 4) If customer needs quicker rollback, run optimizer-toggle --tenant brightpost --force-quant-off which reverts quantization immediately but preserves batch cache. 5) If latency persists after quant demote, reduce adaptive-batcher max-batch-size to 8 and set dynamic_queue=false for the route. 6) Engineering to open root cause PR for INT8 kernel ordering and schedule a non-production repro and patch.
Follow-up: Engineering will test a quant-kernel fix; customer to be kept informed via thread. Ticket to be updated with postmortem link once fix merges.
